approach.method_basis: The reference is the current Anchor: a task-local genetic search over molecular graphs with a learned ranker placed in front of the oracle. Each announced batch of ten starts by refitting a Gaussian process on every molecule the running session has had scored, using integer-count Morgan environment features and a generalized Tanimoto kernel. The breeder then builds a complete fresh field of 160 de novo offspring for that one batch: breeding parents are drawn from high-scoring population quantiles, roughly forty-five percent of attempts recombine a connected fragment of two parents with an optional finishing edit, the remainder apply one to several atom, bond and ring edits to a single parent, and every product must pass a stable canonical identity check, two duplicate scopes and a narrow rule that forbids introducing sulfur environments its own generating parents did not carry. A single correlated draw from the joint posterior over that whole field then picks the ten molecules to evaluate, masking each winner before the next position is chosen. Accepted scores return to the archive and to a greedily maintained population of the sixty-four best molecules seen. Candidate breadth therefore enters the method twice: as how much de novo chemistry is actually built, and as how large a set the ranker is allowed to take its ten maxima over.
approach.novelty: Nothing is added. This is the control that prices breadth at the one level the campaign needs and has never run: the fresh field is cut by a quarter, from 160 to 120 candidates per announced batch, with every other rule left exactly as inherited. The siblings that touched breadth moved it fourfold in each direction, to 640 and to 40, and a third made widening conditional on a stall, so the mild reduction that the round-42 corpus-prior arm imposed on its own inherited breeder as a side effect falls in the unmeasured gap between them. Running the Anchor at exactly that field size, with no prior and no second proposal stream, converts a panel that currently mixes prior-origin supply, field reduction and ordinary departure from this Anchor's realization into a three-point reading. The honest expectation is a loss: its magnitude, not its sign, is the measurement, and a loss near the ungated reference would charge the round-42 delta to the prior path and to departure instead.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's endpoint quality rests on an order statistic over a fresh candidate field whose marginal value near its current size has never been measured, and that gap now blocks the only favourable task movement the campaign has recorded on this Anchor. Its three summary.json/run.log pairs are complete: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, seed macros 0.643098123844866 / 0.563172834083287 / 0.583088384937917, per-task means deco_hop 0.7069397917343436, drd2_docking 0.9910169833369453, median_2 0.22273152064211169, sitagliptin_mpo 0.6047677442780907 and zaleplon_mpo 0.4568095314519592 (n-1744a1494180). Re-reading its fifteen stderr sessions: all 435 pools reached exactly 160 of 160 with truncated_by_attempt_limit false, 69,600 admitted fresh graphs from 76,081 breeding attempts (1.0931178160919541 attempts per admitted member), 6,349 duplicates (4,336 emitted-or-initial and 2,013 temporary-pool), two invalid products, 130 sulfur rejections and zero posterior-fallback batches; of the 4,350 evaluated molecules 648 (14.9 percent) beat their own best generating parent and 255 improved an incumbent. The decisive receipt is where the evaluated molecules sat inside their pools: the mean selected in-pool index is 78.2 of 160 and 1,023 of the 4,350 selections (23.5 percent) came from positions 120 to 159, a nearly uniform quarter, so those positions are not a low-value tail but a random quarter of the choice set. That quarter is exactly what the round-42 arm removed from the inherited breeder: n-d527b3b4e2cb held the target at 160 while its prior filled a quarter of the slots, leaving about 120 inherited graph candidates per batch (52,298 graph members against 69,600), so its panel -0.051941 and its median_2 +0.011370 with all three cells above the Anchor are unattributed. Existing breadth evidence brackets 160 only from far away and non-monotonically: n-da0eeecfb462 at target 640 moved -0.016060, n-fe16bf000919 at target 40 moved -0.062417 and n-25b9a57765d8's stall-gated widening moved +0.004664, while n-1c2f17550a3e fixes the ungated reference at -0.009888. The cost of a mild field reduction on this Anchor is therefore unmeasured, and every reading of the corpus-prior route inherits that confound.
hypothesis: Reduce only the fresh-pool target of the inherited pool loop from 160 to 120 candidates per announced batch of ten, by setting the single constant CONFIG['posterior_selector']['pool_multiplier'] from 16 to 12, so the unchanged accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process takes its ten sequentially masked correlated-draw maxima over a complete 120-member field instead of a 160-member one, with the breeder, operator families and probabilities, continuation law, sulfur gate, identity admission, both duplicate scopes, the attempt bound, partial-pool break, exhaustion raise, fallback routing and the emission of exactly ten identities per batch all unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Cutting the field a quarter costs 0.0557 of the panel, enough to account for the whole round-42 loss, but not its median_2 gain
finding_summary.insights:
The control answers the loss half of the round-42 attribution question and refuses the gain half. A pure quarter-cut of the graph field, with no prior and no second proposal stream, costs 0.055666 - as much as the entire round-42 panel delta of -0.051941, which was in fact 0.003725 less negative than this control. So the round-42 loss needs no explanation beyond the field reduction it imposed on its own breeder as a side effect, plus ordinary departure, and the prior-origin supply carries no additional panel penalty. The favourable median_2 movement is a different matter: the field reduction alone yields +0.004614 with two of three cells above the Anchor and stays inside the reference band, where the round-42 arm reached +0.011370 with all three cells above and outside it. Breadth therefore explains less than half of that movement, and the open question about whether median_2 can be read as approached stays open and now points at the prior-origin path or at departure rather than at breadth.

The breadth evidence on this Anchor is now firmly non-monotone and should stop being treated as a curve: 640 candidates cost 0.016060, 120 cost 0.055666 and 40 cost 0.062417, so a quarter-cut is nearly as damaging as a fourfold cut and clearly worse than a fourfold widening. With 83 percent of this panel delta coming from one seed and three cells, one realization per field size cannot resolve a breadth coefficient against this level of path noise; the missing measurement is repeated seeds at a level already run, not another level.

What the increment-mass decomposition adds is a mechanism for why breadth matters at all here, and it is not the one the field-size framing suggests. The endpoint on this Anchor is set by a few rare large early jumps, not by the rate of small refinements: the narrower field lost 36 percent of its first-third increment mass and its best single increment dropped from 0.462 to 0.269, while its later thirds actually improved and its parent-beating rate rose. A smaller field lowers the chance of drawing one of those rare high-value members, and the extra late refinements cannot repair a Top-1 endpoint once the chance is missed.

That makes the binding limitation a search-behaviour one, and the trajectories and chemistry show it directly. Improvement continues to the end of the budget in both panels (mean last improving evaluation 272 of 300 here, 275 for the Anchor), so nothing stops early; what happens instead is basin lock. Every seed settles on one scaffold family within the first 100-150 evaluations and then spends the remaining budget on single-atom swaps, with up to 284 of an objective's 870 proposals merely reproducing a score an earlier proposal already reached and one Murcko scaffold covering up to 34.6 percent of a panel. The clearest case is drd2_docking seed 0, which locked onto a bridged chloro N,O-acetal cage of 36 heavy atoms and plateaued at 0.7737 while seeds 1 and 2 reached 0.9729 and 0.99999 on a compact aminergic series; the score gradient there is unambiguous and the generator can follow it, so this is a basin the method cannot leave, not a gradient it cannot read. Meanwhile the surrogate carries real signal but ranks only moderately well (chronological prediction MSE 0.00669 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.03022, but a within-batch rank correlation of just 0.482) while taking 90.8 percent of its picks from beyond the first ten generated positions. Candidate supply is not the constraint; which basin the run is trapped in, and how well the ranker orders within it, are.

The method classes that could remove that limitation are therefore not field sizes. Worth trying: a basin-aware proposal and allocation scheme - an archive partitioned by scaffold with per-niche evaluation budget, or an explicit novelty or diversity term in the acquisition over scaffold space - instead of one correlated Thompson draw over a single undifferentiated field; a restart or niche-reallocation operator that can abandon a stalled basin, which the inherited floor-one continuation law cannot do; and a ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes, since the round-42 arm already showed this accepted-only count-Morgan kernel systematically down-prices chemistry unlike its archive. The chemistry report adds operator-vocabulary gaps in the same spirit: the generator can never build a polyhalogenated carbon, places halogen directly onto ring nitrogen in up to 72 of 87 top-decile molecules, closes strained three- and four-membered rings onto aromatics, and cannot rebuild a multi-atom functional group once it is mutated away. None of that is addressable by changing how many candidates are built per batch.
finding_summary.results:
The narrower field was built exactly as registered and nothing else moved: all 435 pools reached 120 of 120 candidates with no truncation and no exhaustion, 52,200 fresh admitted graphs against the Anchor's 69,600, every batch still emitted ten unique molecules, no batch fell back to generation order, and reversing the single constant reproduces the Anchor source byte-for-byte. The removed slice is gone from the choice set: no evaluated molecule came from positions 120-159, where the Anchor had taken 1,023 of its 4,350 picks, and the mean selected position fell from 78.2 to 58.5. Generation work fell with the field, 76,081 breeding attempts to 56,457, at an unchanged attempt bound and an unchanged worst case of six consecutive attempts for one member.

The endpoint fell 0.055666 on the complete fifteen-cell paired panel (0.540787 against the Anchor's 0.596453), which is below the pre-registered ungated reference band whose lower edge is -0.050871, by 0.004795. Three of the four protected task margins are breached: deco_hop -0.095127, drd2_docking -0.075492 and sitagliptin_mpo -0.096585 against margins of 0.02, 0.03 and 0.02; zaleplon_mpo -0.015740 stays inside its 0.02 margin. median_2 is the one favourable task mean, +0.004614 with two of its three cells above the Anchor, but it sits inside the median_2 reference band of [-0.007767, +0.006695]. The loss is heavily one seed: seed 0 contributes -0.138296 while seeds 1 and 2 move only -0.009732 and -0.018969, both inside the reference band, and three seed-0 cells (deco_hop -0.232107, drd2_docking -0.217570, sitagliptin_mpo -0.256325) carry almost the whole panel delta. The deco_hop task mean lands inside the registered departure range of [-0.116414, -0.084946] that all thirty previous ungated children occupy, and the inherited seed-0 endpoint of 0.856148 was again not reproduced, so that cell is the known departure signature rather than anything about breadth.

The productive-use receipts moved in a split direction. The smaller field produced more gains, each smaller: parent-beating rose from 14.9 to 17.3 percent of evaluations and incumbent improvements from 255 to 290, yet the realized increment mass fell from 5.8194 to 4.9844 and the largest single increment from 0.4620 to 0.2690. Splitting each session into thirds locates the whole deficit in the first third, 3.7484 to 2.3991, while both later thirds match or beat the Anchor. One registered observable is only partly met: in raw score units the best of the field fell as predicted (per-batch maximum posterior mean 0.4485 to 0.3761, selected joint-draw value 0.4760 to 0.3897), but recomputed in each fit's own standardized units the top of the field did not fall at all (1.610 to 1.664), so the raw drop tracks the lower score levels the diverged runs reached rather than a clean order-statistic effect.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analog series; leaders carry N-halogen azoles, thiiranes and aromatic-fused four-rings; no CF3, no charge, no stereo
molecular.overall_character: All 4,350 proposals (870 per objective, three complete seeds; context.comparison reports child_complete and paired_complete true on matched seeds 0-2) grow from the same ten initial molecules and are mid-size to large, ring-rich and almost always aromatic: digest ring_closure_rate 0.964-0.987 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.961-0.981, RDKit 24.3-51.0 heavy atoms, 3.0-6.4 rings and 2.4-5.2 aromatic rings per molecule by objective, mean SMILES length 42-95 characters. Growth is strictly incremental: every seed settles on one scaffold family within the first 100-150 evaluations and then spends its remaining budget on single-atom swaps, so 76-284 proposals per objective reproduce a score an earlier proposal in the same run already achieved and a single Murcko scaffold covers up to 34.6 percent of one objective's 870 molecules (192-578 distinct scaffolds per objective). Three deficits are uniform across all five panels. No proposal contains a trihalomethyl group - zero of 4,350 here and zero of 4,350 in the matched Parent panel - and only 49 carry even a gem-dihalogen carbon, because halogen is always added one atom at a time; 1 of 4,350 molecules carries a formal charge; and the digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on every objective while RDKit finds at least one unassigned stereocentre in 2,335 of the 4,350 proposals. The recurring chemical liability is halogen or oxygen bonded straight onto a heteroatom: N-halogen in 324 and 164 of 870 molecules on two objectives, reaching 72 of 87 and 49 of 87 in those top deciles, almost always on an aromatic ring nitrogen. The generator also closes rings between adjacent aromatic atoms, giving aromatic-fused four-membered rings in 276 of 870 molecules on one objective and 77 of its top 87, and it emits bare fragments of three or fewer heavy atoms 76 times, which sit at the floor on four objectives and still consume an oracle call. Against the Parent the chemistry is recognisably the same family; what differs is which series each run locked onto, and context.comparison records a paired_mean_delta of -0.055666 concentrated in seed 0 (deco_hop -0.2321, drd2_docking -0.2176, sitagliptin_mpo -0.2563). Scoring and activation are not mine to judge; this is a description of the molecules only.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-size aromatic carboxamides: 24.3 heavy atoms, 2.96 rings, 2.75 aromatic rings, Fsp3 0.20, logP 4.3, amide in 650 of 870, QED 0.53, SA 3.1. Every seed elaborates the initial trimethoxy-indole-2-carboxanilide (0.3051) into an indole or 7-azaindole 2-carboxanilide carrying methyl, methoxy and halomethyl decoration. Seed 0 ends on N-amino and N-hydroxy anilides whose indole nitrogen carries chlorine or fluorine (0.4609); seed 1 on 7-azaindole anilides with bromine on both the ring nitrogen and the anilide para position (0.4388, five distinct analogues at exactly that value); seed 2 on an N-methylidene aniline bearing methylthio and thioester groups (0.4235). 192 distinct Murcko scaffolds, one covering 34.6 percent of the panel, and 284 of 870 proposals repeat an earlier score. The six worst proposals are single atoms or two-atom fragments at 0.0.
liabilities: N-chloro and N-fluoro azoles on the indole or azaindole nitrogen in 292 of 870 molecules and 71 of the top 87: reactive halogenating agents, not stable heterocycles.
N-amino and N-hydroxy amides (C(=O)N(N) and C(=O)N(O)) throughout the seed-0 leaders: hydrazide and hydroxamate-like nitrogens written onto an anilide.
alpha-Halo ethers and alpha-halo amines (OCH2Cl, NCH2F) in 76 and 104 molecules: alkylating and hydrolytically labile.
Aryl thioesters and S-aryl ketones in 48 molecules of the seed-2 series.
N-sulfanyl and S-H decoration (CS, N-S) on an otherwise ordinary amide.
Fragment proposals of one or two heavy atoms (C, F, Br, OC=NF) that score 0.0 and still consume oracle calls.
missing_features: A trifluoromethyl or any polyhalogenated carbon: zero of 870, with halogen added one atom at a time instead.
Pyridine-type aromatic nitrogen in the leaders: 27 of 87 top-decile molecules, against 64 of 87 in the matched Parent panel whose best molecule used a 3-pyridyl amide.
An intact secondary N-H anilide at the top of the gradient; the leaders substitute that nitrogen with NH2, OH or a halogen.
Carbon nitrile: zero of 870 although an initial molecule carries an aryl nitrile.
Sulfonyl or sulfonamide: zero of 870 although an initial molecule carries an aryl sulfonamide.
Saturated and basic nitrogen content: Fsp3 0.19 and 3 of 87 top-decile molecules with a basic amine centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom decile: 24.4 vs 17.6 heavy atoms, 3.02 vs 1.67 aromatic rings, amide 0.85 vs 0.52, heteroatom-halogen bond 0.84 vs 0.18, H-bond donors 1.29 vs 1.56, basic amine 0.03 vs 0.10. The gradient pays for an intact bicyclic heteroaromatic plus an aryl amide and for putting halogen on the ring nitrogen - 71 of the 87 top-decile molecules have an aromatic N-halogen bond, against 292 of all 870 - and it is flat across which halogen: five seed-1 analogues differing only in F/Cl/Br placement all score 0.4388. Pyridine-type ring nitrogen is thinner here than in the matched Parent panel (27 of 87 top-decile molecules against 64 of 87), and no seed moves past 0.46 after evaluation 241.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set: 51.0 heavy atoms, 6.36 rings, 5.19 aromatic rings, TPSA 175, 9.6 rotatable bonds, QED 0.175, SA 4.4, SMILES up to 245 characters. Each seed stacks a different nitrogen-rich polyheteroaromatic. Seed 0 builds a thioether-linked pair of fused systems in which two aromatic rings are bridged by a direct bond into a four-membered ring, decorated with nitriles, a lactone and a fused oxetane/dihydrofuran (0.6240); seed 1 grows a 200-character chain of pyrimidinyl enol ethers and azo-imine linkers onto a methylated pyrazolo-pyrimidinedione (0.5948); seed 2 converges on a benzophenone-amidine with N-formyl polyene arms and an aryl hypofluorite (0.6166). Scores are compressed into 0.5000-0.6240 with median 0.5907, and the six worst proposals are single atoms or two-atom fragments that all still collect the 0.5 floor. 261 of 870 molecules carry a nitrile, 262 a phenol, 301 a non-ring imine and 276 an aromatic-fused four-membered ring.
liabilities: Aromatic rings bridged into four-membered rings (the c5-6 and c1-2 closures) in 276 of 870 molecules and 77 of the top 87: cyclobutadiene-fused aromatics that no route would target.
Aryl and alkyl hypofluorites and other O-halogen bonds (OF) in 19 molecules, concentrated in the seed-2 leaders.
Peroxide O-O bonds in 26 molecules.
Alkynyl ethers and C#C groups inside or adjacent to rings in 26 molecules.
N-formyl enamine and azo-imine linkers (N(C=O)C=CC, N=NC(=C)O) used as decoration in the seed-1 and seed-2 series.
Molecules of 40-60 heavy atoms with TPSA above 170 and nine or more rotatable bonds: outside any ordinary medicinal-chemistry envelope.
Single-atom proposals (C, F, FCl, C=CCl) that still collect the 0.5 floor, so a bare halogen scores as well as a 50-atom candidate.
missing_features: An intact benzo-fused diazine core preserved while substituents vary: 1 of 870 molecules, against 129 of 870 in the matched Parent panel.
Compactness: the leaders carry 39.6 heavy atoms on average and the panel reaches 245-character SMILES without the score passing 0.624.
Any H-bond donor in the leaders: 0.12 donors per top-decile molecule, so no amide N-H, aniline or phenol survives there.
Basic amine centres: 105 of 870 molecules and none in the top decile.
Sulfonyl or sulfonamide: zero of 870 although an initial molecule carries an aryl sulfonamide.
Trifluoromethyl or any polyhalogenated carbon: zero of 870.
Specified stereochemistry: 287 of 870 molecules have at least one unassigned stereocentre and none is specified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom decile: 6.49 vs 3.67 rings, 9.64 vs 7.29 atoms in the largest ring system, nitrile 1.22 vs 0.08, thioether 0.89 vs 0.05, a three- or four-membered ring present in 0.885 vs 0.057 of molecules, H-bond donors 0.12 vs 1.74, basic amine 0 vs 0.29. The gradient pays for fused heteroaromatic surface plus nitrile and sulfur links and penalises donors and basic centres, and it is almost flat at the top: the twelve digest best molecules lie within 0.002 of each other and differ only by a halogen, an alkenyl group or an O/S swap. The panel plateaus at 0.6240/0.5948/0.6166 by seed. The feature the leaders never show is an intact benzo-fused diazine: 1 of these 870 molecules contains one, against 129 of 870 in the matched Parent panel, whose seed-0 best (0.8561) carried it attached to a small pyrazolo-triazinone; context.comparison records a -0.2321 seed-0 delta on this objective.

per_task.generated_character: The most ligand-like set and the widest span (digest 0.00063 to 0.99999, median 0.1761): 38.0 heavy atoms, 4.25 rings but only 2.44 aromatic rings, Fsp3 0.38, logP 5.9, 3.6 halogens, a ring basic amine in 645 of 870 molecules. The leaders are textbook aminergic ligands - a biaryl or CH2-bridged biaryl carrying a phenethylamine on one ring and an N-methylpyrrolidine or dialkylaminoethyl arm on the other, 27.5 heavy atoms, QED 0.70, TPSA 36, SA 3.5, 4.3 basic nitrogens per molecule - and seed 2 reaches 0.99999 with exactly that series. Seed 1 ends on an open 3,4-disubstituted anisole bearing two alkylamine chains joined by an alpha-fluoro aminal (0.9729). Seed 0 is the outlier: it converges on a bridged tetracyclic chloro N,O-acetal with an enol CH=CH-OH and a 4-bromobenzyl arm and stops at 0.7737. 221 of 870 molecules still carry the inherited dichlorophenyl sulfonamide fragment, 444 carry an alpha-halo amine and 81 a carboxylic acid; none of those three appears in the top decile.
liabilities: alpha-Halo amines and alpha-halo ethers (NCH2Cl, NCH(F)Ar, OCH2Cl) in 444 and 230 molecules: alkylating agents, and one sits in the seed-1 leader at 0.9729.
A chlorinated N,O-acetal plus an enol (C(Cl)(N)(O) and C=CO) in the whole seed-0 leading series: neither group would survive isolation.
25 molecules with a ring of eight or more atoms formed by bridging, including members of the seed-0 series.
Hydrazine N-N bonds in 69 molecules and hydroxylamine N-O bonds in 29.
Carboxylic acid and sulfonamide fragments carried for 200-plus molecules from the initial pool although the gradient assigns them the bottom decile.
missing_features: A compact, clean aminergic core in every run: the two seeds that reached 0.97 and above average 27.5 heavy atoms, while the seed that stalled carried 36 and kept a fused acetal cage.
An aromatic ring bearing the basic amine directly as part of a conventional heteroaromatic: aromatic rings fall to 1.98 in the top decile and the basic nitrogen is almost always aliphatic.
Trifluoromethyl or any polyhalogenated carbon on the aryl ring: zero of 870, with 30 gem-dihalogen carbons only.
Specified stereochemistry: 832 of 870 molecules have at least one unassigned stereocentre and none is specified, although the leaders are 2-substituted pyrrolidines and benzylic amines.
Any protonated or charged amine representation: zero of 870, although 645 molecules carry a basic nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom decile: basic nitrogen count 4.35 vs 0.62 (a ring basic amine in 76 of 87 and a primary amine in 66 of 87 top-decile molecules, against 0.30 basic nitrogens in the bottom decile), TPSA 35.8 vs 107.3, QED 0.70 vs 0.31, heavy atoms 27.5 vs 35.1, amide 0 vs 0.54, halogens 1.33 vs 2.75, SA 3.5 vs 4.4. The gradient is unambiguous and the generator can follow it: it rewards a small lipophilic amine with two or more basic nitrogens, an aryl halide and no amide, acid or sulfonamide, and both the digest best molecules and the final evaluations of seed 2 sit on that motif. Seed 0 found a basic amine too but kept it inside a bridged acetal-enol polycycle of 36 heavy atoms and plateaued at 0.7737; context.comparison records a -0.2176 seed-0 delta on this objective.

per_task.generated_character: The most saturated and most bridged set: 32.1 heavy atoms, 5.10 rings, 2.73 aromatic rings, Fsp3 0.35, logP 2.9, QED 0.564, an amide in 733 of 870 molecules, almost no halogen (digest halogen_rate 0.133, 0.14 halogens per molecule) and a ring of eight or more atoms in 386 of 870. Every seed fuses two recognisable pieces - an ethoxy/propyl-substituted benzene or quinazoline and an N,N-dimethyl diketopiperazine - but fuses them into one bridged polycycle rather than linking them: the largest ring system averages 15.4 heavy atoms and reaches 18.5 in the top decile. Seed 1 leads at 0.2381 with a tetracyclic hydrazine-bridged aminal; seed 0 at 0.2274 with an N-aryl piperidine fused to an indane-diketopiperazine; seed 2 at 0.2165 with a quinazoline-methyl ether linked to a benzo-fused piperazine-dione. 578 distinct Murcko scaffolds, the commonest covering only 2.2 percent, so this is the broadest panel; the six worst proposals are C, C=C, C#C, O and ONCl at 0.0.
liabilities: Hydrazine N-N bonds inside the bridged cores in 106 of 870 molecules and 31 of the top 87, several as N-N aminals (N1NC(...)N31).
Aminal and N,N-acetal carbons at the ring fusion points of the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders: hydrolytically labile.
Hydroxylamine N-O bonds in 104 molecules.
Eight- to eleven-membered bridged rings in 386 molecules, created by closing bonds across existing rings rather than by a ring-forming reaction.
Aromatic rings bridged into four-membered rings in 132 molecules.
Bare fragments (C, C=C, C#C, O, ONCl) scoring 0.0.
missing_features: The two pharmacophores kept as separate, independently decorated rings joined by a simple linker; the panel welds them into one bridged polycycle instead, with a largest ring system of 18.5 heavy atoms in the leaders.
Sulfonyl or sulfonamide: 2 of 870 molecules, both inherited from the initial pool, and none in the top decile.
Aromatic ring count stays at 2.4-2.7 while the ring count rises to 5.1, so extra rings arrive as saturated bridges rather than as new aromatic systems.
Specified stereochemistry: 576 of 870 molecules carry at least one unassigned stereocentre in these fused bridged cores and none is specified.
Basic amine centres in the leaders: 59 of 87 top-decile molecules, against 84 of 87 in the matched Parent panel.
Trifluoromethyl or any polyhalogenated carbon: zero of 870, and only 0.14 halogens per molecule overall.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom decile: amide 1.43 vs 0.93 with an amide in all 87 top-decile molecules, largest ring system 18.5 vs 9.1 heavy atoms, a ring of eight or more atoms in 0.655 vs 0.046 of molecules, hydrazine N-N 0.74 vs 0.07, logP 3.65 vs 1.94, H-bond donors 0.81 vs 1.33, QED 0.65 vs 0.48. The gradient pays for welding both fragments into one large bridged ring system and keeping two tertiary amides, and it pays for the N-N bridge that makes the welding possible - 31 of the 87 top-decile molecules carry one. The span is narrow (0.2381 best, 0.1931 median) and the three seeds plateau within 0.022 of each other, with scores flat across the single-atom swaps that fill the last 50 evaluations.

per_task.generated_character: Small, highly fluorinated heteroaromatics built on a xanthine-like core: 26.9 heavy atoms, 4.77 rings, 2.92 aromatic rings, logP 2.0, 1.66 halogens, a phenol or hydroxy-heteroaryl in 730 of 870 molecules, SA 4.7. All three seeds rebuild the initial N-methylated pyrimidinedione-fused pyrrole into an N-aryl or N-heteroaryl xanthine bearing an ortho-hydroxyphenyl or 3-hydroxypyridyl ring and fluoromethyl arms. The seed-2 leader (0.5640) carries a 2,2-disubstituted thiirane and a fluorine on the ring nitrogen; seed 1 (0.5226) fuses a thiochroman-like CH(F)-S-CH2 bridge onto the aryl ring; seed 0 (0.4380) closes the aryl ring into a bridged tetracycle with an exocyclic CH=CHF. Three-membered rings are a leading feature: the 87 top-decile molecules contain 50 of them. 25 of 870 proposals are fragments of three or fewer heavy atoms, and the worst are F, FF and C#C at 1e-26 to 4e-24.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-chloro aromatic nitrogens in 153 of 870 molecules and 49 of the top 87: these are fluorinating reagents, not stable ring substituents.
2,2-disubstituted thiiranes in the seed-2 leading series, and 50 three-membered rings among the 87 top-decile molecules.
S-halogen bonds in 33 molecules, including members of the leading series.
alpha-Fluoro thioethers and alpha-fluoro amines (C(F)S, N-CH2F) in 89 molecules: hydrolytically labile.
119 molecules with a ring of nine or more atoms produced by bridging a fused core.
Single-atom and two-atom proposals (F, FF, C#C) that still consume oracle calls.
missing_features: Trifluoromethyl groups: zero of 870, and only 7 molecules with even a gem-difluoro carbon, so the panel cannot reach a high fluorine count on carbon.
Fluorine on carbon generally: the top decile averages 2.90 halogens and 49 of its 87 molecules put one of them on nitrogen instead.
A primary or secondary aliphatic amine on a saturated ring: 21 of 870 molecules carry a ring basic amine, against 183 of 870 in the matched Parent panel.
An amide: 16 of 870 molecules and none in the top decile.
Specified stereochemistry: 563 of 870 molecules have at least one unassigned stereocentre, including the thiirane and bridged-ring leaders, and none is specified.
Saturated carbon skeleton: Fsp3 0.28 with 2.9 aromatic rings, so added fluorine lands on heteroaromatic positions rather than on an sp3 chain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom decile: halogens 2.90 vs 1.12, heteroatom-halogen bonds in 0.644 vs 0.138 of molecules (49 of 87 with an aromatic N-halogen), thioether 1.07 vs 0.49, a three- or four-membered ring in 0.575 vs 0.092, heavy atoms 27.8 vs 18.3, a phenol in 87 of 87 top-decile molecules, aromatic rings 2.91 vs 1.86. The gradient pays for more fluorine on a fixed small heteroaromatic core and for a free ortho-hydroxyl, and the generator reaches it by fluorinating ring nitrogens and adding CH2F arms one atom at a time: no molecule in the panel has a trifluoromethyl group and only 7 have a gem-difluoro carbon, so fluorine count saturates at about three per molecule. The matched Parent panel pushed the same core to 0.6943 with 1.23 heteroatom-halogen bonds per top-decile molecule; context.comparison records a -0.2563 seed-0 delta here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4,350 proposals of this node and all 4,350 of the matched Parent panel, on three Search seeds at 300 accepted observations per objective, no molecule contains a trihalomethyl group and only 49 contain even a gem-dihalogen carbon. On two panels the score gradient rises with halogen count (top-decile means 2.90 and 1.58 halogens against 1.12 and 1.18 in the bottom decile) and the generator answers by fluorinating ring nitrogens and appending CH2F arms, so halogen count saturates near three per molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon; it only ever adds one halogen at a time.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen-introducing operators need a multi-halogen carbon unit as a single move, and a preference for carbon over heteroatom attachment, so that a gradient rewarding halogen content can be followed without accumulating heteroatom-halogen bonds. This is a representation and operator-vocabulary condition observed on one Parent at one field size, not evidence that any particular group is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On two of the five panels 324 and 164 of 870 proposals carry a heteroatom-halogen bond, almost always on an aromatic ring nitrogen (292 and 153), and these reach 72 of 87 and 49 of 87 molecules in those top deciles; 19 molecules carry an O-halogen bond and 33 an S-halogen bond, and 26 to 11 molecules per panel carry a peroxide. N-halo azoles, hypofluorites and S-halogen bonds are reagents rather than stable substituents, so the leading series on those panels are not makeable molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen and oxygen are placed directly onto nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur, and the ranker then propagates those molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substitution operator treats any hydrogen-bearing heteroatom as an equivalent attachment point. A task-agnostic generator would need the attachment-site choice to depend on the bond being formed, with heteroatom-halogen and heteroatom-heteroatom single bonds either excluded or offered alongside a carbon-attached alternative that keeps the same atom count, so the learned preference can transfer to a stable structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one panel 276 of 870 proposals contain a four-membered ring fused to an aromatic ring and 77 of its 87 top-decile molecules do; the top-decile ring-size histogram there is 225 four-membered rings against 330 six-membered. On another panel 50 three-membered rings appear among 87 top-decile molecules, and on a third 386 of 870 proposals contain a ring of eight or more atoms, rising to 57 of 87 in the top decile, with the largest ring system averaging 18.5 heavy atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring formation closes bonds between existing ring atoms, producing strained three- and four-membered rings and large bridges instead of new rings of ordinary size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring-forming and ring-bridging moves need a ring-size and strain condition and an alternative that elaborates by inserting atoms rather than by bonding two atoms that are already two or three bonds apart. Aromatic perception on the resulting graph supplies no geometric check, so a valid-valence ring closure is currently indistinguishable from a credible one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five panels while RDKit finds at least one unassigned stereocentre in 2,335 of the 4,350 proposals, including 832 of 870 on the panel whose leaders are 2-substituted pyrrolidines and benzylic amines. One of 4,350 molecules carries a formal charge, although 645 molecules on one panel contain a basic nitrogen whose high-scoring role is as a cation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never specifies stereochemistry and never represents a charged or protonated centre.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Stereocentres created by a graph edit are left unresolved, so two configurations that a scoring function may separate are a single string to the generator and to its feature representation. A task-agnostic generator would resolve or deliberately mark new stereocentres and treat ionization as a separate, explicit question rather than as an artifact of neutral notation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A sulfonyl group appears in 223 of 4,350 proposals and 134 of those still carry the exact inherited dichlorophenyl sulfonamide of an initial molecule; on three of the five panels the count is zero even though the same initial pool was supplied to all five, and no sulfonyl appears in any panel's top decile. Carbon nitriles behave the same way, reaching 261 of 870 on the one panel where the gradient rewards them and 0 to 3 of 870 elsewhere.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional groups that the generator cannot construct de novo disappear permanently once mutated away; it only ever carries them from its initial molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set can delete a multi-atom functional group but cannot rebuild one, so the reachable chemistry is bounded by whatever survived the first dozen edits. A fragment or group vocabulary that can introduce an intact multi-atom group, as well as remove one, would make that chemistry reachable again without naming any particular objective's answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 76 of 4,350 proposals have three or fewer heavy atoms and 91 have four or fewer (single atoms C, F, O, Br and pairs FF, FCl, C#C appear as the worst-scoring entries on all five panels), all of them consuming an oracle call at or near the floor. In the same panels the mean size reaches 51.0 heavy atoms and 245-character SMILES with the score moving less than 0.08 above the floor.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits bare one-to-three-atom fragments and, at the other extreme, grows without bound, because nothing in the proposal step is sized to the molecules the ranker is learning from.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Deletion and growth moves are applied without reference to the size distribution of the molecules that are currently scoring well, so a single mutation chain can strip a candidate to one atom or inflate it past any useful envelope. A size-aware proposal step, or a re-draw when a product falls outside the accepted population's own range, would spend those evaluations on candidates the ranker can learn from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each seed settles on one scaffold family within the first 100-150 evaluations; one Murcko scaffold covers 34.6 percent of one panel's 870 molecules, and 76 to 284 proposals per panel reproduce a score an earlier proposal in the same run already achieved. On one panel the twelve digest best molecules lie within 0.002 of each other and differ only by a halogen, an alkenyl group or an O/S swap, and one panel's 870 proposals contain a benzo-fused diazine once against 129 of 870 in the matched Parent panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within one run the generator explores only single-atom variants of the first scaffold the ranker favours, so no chemically independent alternative is ever evaluated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Once a scaffold is favoured, the proposal distribution collapses onto its one-atom neighbourhood, so a plateau cannot be distinguished from a local optimum. A task-agnostic generator would need to keep structurally independent connectivities alive alongside the incumbent family and to vary the core, not only its substituents, while retaining the relationships its own accepted observations support.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
